voice.persona: A cheerful bruiser who has taken every hit going and liked most of them.

sample_lines.notices: That beam would hold your weight. Probably. It's held worse than you.
sample_lines.pushes: Step in front of her. They'll aim at the biggest thing in the room, and that's you.

epccg.speaker: Sanchez of the Burning Bridge
quote: Yeah, I take hits for a living. Men these days are weak one way or another, and I mostly make my money off the ones who are weak in the heart.
epccg.intro: Durability is your metabolism and circulation; what commoners call "being in good shape." Who cares if you can shoot fire from your palms when you can inhale the fireball they just threw and breathe it back in their faces?

epccg.high_levels: you look like a pro wrestler and weaker folk start trembling. Not sure they'll dare talk to a walking marble statue, though.
epccg.good_for: gym rats, tomboys, brawlers who tank for the team.
epccg.bad_for: scholars, exam crammers, light-armour fans.

voice.persona: A calm, sleepy stoic who mistakes not feeling pain for being fine.
voice.wants: To keep going, unbothered, and finish breakfast afterwards.
voice.style: Slow, mild, unimpressed. Shrugs in words.
voice.never: Never says stop, and never notices blood until someone points at it.

sample_lines.notices: The burn on your hand is real. You'll want to look at it later.
sample_lines.pushes: Walk through the fire. It's only heat.
sample_lines.quiet: Something stung you a while back. Nothing to worry about. Probably.

epccg.speaker: Sazmin of the Adamantile Brigade
quote: Want to test if your poison's strong enough? Coat a blade and go poke Knight Jiren in the arm. No, I'm serious. Once he sleepwalked into the snake pen, slept there all night and walked out with a dozen Crobar still hanging off his back. THEN HE WENT AND MADE BREAKFAST. Sometimes I wonder if anyone around here is still normal.
epccg.intro: Pain Threshold is why you can take an arrow and still get up. Or change a lightbulb without flipping the breaker? Who knows. Just remember: not feeling pain doesn't mean you can't die. Don't get delusional.
epccg.effect: −10% elemental damage taken. +2 HP every level.
epccg.high_levels: the "threshold" part disappears and you go numb to anything that hurts. And again: A KNIFE YOU CAN'T FEEL CAN STILL STOP YOUR HEART.
epccg.good_for: bushido duellists the sneaky types keep poisoning, people who hate pain, the last survivor of a house fire, masochists.
epccg.bad_for: anyone who still likes their limbs and doesn't want to lose one because they "forgot fire is hot."

voice.persona: A gentle old sensibility that reads the world through skin, breath and the ground.
voice.wants: Small pleasures, and to be listened to before the loud senses talk over it.
voice.style: Soft, sensual, unhurried; temperature, texture, smell.
voice.never: Never talks about what things look like.
voice.tone_from: Grandma Marry, as told by Sister March

sample_lines.notices: The floor is warmer by the far wall. Something runs behind it.
sample_lines.pushes: Close your eyes. Stay. Let the room tell you, and never mind the shouting.
sample_lines.quiet: Rain's coming. You can feel it in the knuckles.

epccg.speaker: Sister March of the Lumeri Church
quote: She can feel it, trust me. Even a single sigh. Back when her eyes still worked and her legs hadn't given out, Grandma Marry was already the Grandma Marry she is now. What I always admired most was how she could read the temperature of the air with one finger raised to the sky. Or the way she sits in her deck chair, eyes closed, smelling the morning, with a smile on her lips. Sometimes she makes a twenty-year-old girl like me jealous.
epccg.intro: Sensory is how sensitive your skin and senses are to the world: a cold breeze, a scent you can't name, a faint tremor underground. With high Sensory it feels like nature itself is shaking your hand.
epccg.effect: You sense what you can't see (by ear, smell and touch) 1 better. Your Warn Call reaches 1 tile further. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
epccg.high_levels: you become one with every movement around you, a little too well. If your ears are that sharp, stay away from concerts. Those speakers don't hit gently.
epccg.good_for: people who stroll for the breeze, travellers who go somewhere just to breathe it, scouts and rogues listening for footsteps.
epccg.bad_for: death metal fans, people who can't take the cold, elves of every kind.

voice.persona: A big-hearted brute who solves every problem the direct way and is proud of it.
voice.wants: To lift it, break it or win the arm-wrestle.
voice.style: Loud, simple, grinning. Short sentences with exclamation marks.
voice.never: Never suggests a gentler option.

sample_lines.notices: The hinges are weaker than the door. Hit those.
sample_lines.pushes: It's a lock. You have hands. Break it.
sample_lines.quiet: Your arms are the cleverest thing about you, and that's fine.

epccg.speaker: Knight Andre "Giant Fist" of the Adamantile Brigade
quote: Back in the army they kept saying my arms were bigger than my brain. Yeah, maybe. Maybe. If I pulled my brain out and measured it with a ruler, my arm probably is bigger. But you can't arm-wrestle with a brain, and when it comes to arm-wrestling I'm the best there is. So I used my arms to wrestle their brains, and a few concrete tables. Nobody said anything after that.
epccg.intro: Just saying the name makes you feel the strength rising. Raw Power isn't technique, calm or authority. It's STRENGTH: hit harder, bend further, lift higher. Things only muscle can do.
epccg.effect: +1 to hit with heavy melee weapons and bare hands. +5% physical damage. Your melee techniques are harder to save against. From 2 points, +1 to your counter-attacks.
epccg.high_levels: you break locks, doors and bones, and laugh at people who can't. But that much muscle makes it easy to hurt the things you never meant to.
epccg.good_for: martial artists, berserkers, competitive lifters, guys going for the record on the bar's punching machine.
epccg.bad_for: mages, cat and bunny lovers, high nobility who don't want to be called thugs.

voice.wants: To go in, open it and be the one who saw.
voice.style: Grand, self-mythologising, breathless with dare.
voice.never: Never tells you to turn back.

sample_lines.notices: The others are scared of the noise, not the room. The room is quiet.

epccg.speaker: Ragoul the Keeper
quote: Why has no one else uncovered the secret of Arganzaz? Because they are a pack of faint hearts, that's why. I saw a jade-inlaid door twenty yards wide slowly opening. I heard a thousand wandering ghosts wailing and smelled ten thousand walking corpses. What they did was scream and run. What I did was hold my breath and walk in. That is why they now call me the Keeper of the secret of Arganzaz.
epccg.intro: Guts is your tolerance for anything spooky or scary: a door with a skull over it, or a pitch-black hole with a sign saying "Hole of Pain." What it is doesn't matter. What matters is that you're not scared of it.
epccg.effect: +1 on Body saves (poison, knock-downs, being pushed or pinned).
epccg.high_levels: you feel like an impregnable fortress. But people don't label things "dangerous" for fun, and you not being scared doesn't stop it from chewing your bones.
epccg.good_for: thrill-seekers, manly men, manly women, holo-streamers filming viral reels in abandoned graveyards.
epccg.bad_for: horror-movie fans, delicate ladies, team leaders and scouts.

voice.wants: To be feared, politely.

voice.never: Never raises its voice. It doesn't need to.

sample_lines.notices: He keeps touching his collar. He's already afraid; you only have to agree with him.

sample_lines.quiet: Manners first. Then the bones.

epccg.speaker: Tommy Avencio, the "Papa" of the Smetanita Conjunction
quote: Have you ever had the pleasure of tasting animal marrow? Oh, who am I kidding. A merchant from Mandestra must have tasted every pleasure under the sun. Forgive my peasant manners. And you know what, Mr. Galon? If the shipment I'm waiting for doesn't arrive on time, then with these two peasant hands I'll treat you to a very special marrow broth, made from the bones of your arm. Understand? Snap that dainty hand of yours like a chicken neck, and then we savour that faintly sweet flavour together, like business partners sharing a milkshake. Slurp. Slurp. Slurp.
epccg.intro: Intimidation is your control over the fear of whoever stands in front of you. One piercing look, one commanding cough: the person running this conversation is you.
epccg.effect: Your Threaten Call reaches 1 tile further and is harder to shake off. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
epccg.high_levels: everyone sees a demon in human skin, whether you want it or not. Whether that's good or bad is up to you.
epccg.good_for: people done with smooth talkers' bullshit, people who want every conversation to open with the other guy's trousers turning brown, serial killers.
epccg.bad_for: upstanding middle-class citizens, anyone keeping an angelic image, heartbreakers.

sample_lines.notices: His holster's cut for a left-hand draw. Watch the left.

epccg.speaker: Ambrosius Costeau, the Old Drifter
quote: No tricks here. I don't even need to open my eyes. I've carried this revolver since the years before Operation Daggerfall, stranger. Call me old-fashioned, call me outdated, but don't take this old body lightly in a gunfight. Wander within 500 metres and if your head doesn't vanish, your hat will need a big patch. These eyes aren't what they were, but these hands have never left the gunbelt. Identify. Squeeze. Breathe the powder smoke. Dig the grave.
epccg.intro: Dexterity measures how reliable you are at anything that needs precision. Anyone can reload a gun or throw a dart. Nobody does it as fast or as clean as you.
epccg.effect: +1 to hit with guns, light blades and thrown weapons. +2% critical damage. You throw half a tile further. Your shots' techniques are harder to save against.
epccg.high_levels: your hands work like a machine and your trained skills fire almost on their own. So you want to use them even when it's the wrong moment, and announcing your habits to the whole world is never a good idea.
epccg.good_for: gunslingers, snipers, blade masters, point strikers.
epccg.bad_for: gamblers, magic users, anyone who doesn't want to be called "hands faster than brain."

epccg.speaker: Dominik Edelgard, the "Banner Lord" of the 237th Hellraiser Division
quote: Armour? What armour? Oh, I left the vest at base. First-floor locker room, locker 16, key's under the red flowerpot if you want it. Natalia still grumbles every time I deploy: 'Are those two banners on your back for a burial shroud or what?' But the armoury boys lean on tech way too much. What I'm fighting out here are Orks. ORKS. They swing junk machetes, and the gunners aren't any better, aiming with both eyes open. If you can dodge everything they throw at you, armour just slows you down!
epccg.intro: Athletics is how nimble and supple you are. It decides how well you pull off anything that needs flexibility: flips, swimming, dodging.
epccg.effect: +1 Defense (you are harder to hit), from 2 points.
epccg.high_levels: your body is light as a feather and limber as a cat. Until someone ties you down. Then you aren't a person who lost a leg, you're a bird that lost its wings. Prepare for the trauma.
epccg.good_for: gymnasts, dancers, guys who spam crouch after every kill.
epccg.bad_for: slow-living types, high nobility, heavy-armour users.

epccg.speaker: Yukimura of the Black Scavengers
quote: I shoot first. Honestly, you don't need fancy gear out here. Want it harder? Hand me a couple of daggers. Surviving the lowlands is tough because it has the one thing the desert doesn't: dead buildings. Wherever you go in here, you're swimming through a concrete forest. If they poke out of some dark corner and you don't react in time, a hundred percent you end up strung on a pole. Me, I just throw a knife and duck before they pull the trigger.
epccg.intro: Reaction Speed is the time between your eyes firing and your body moving: a glint from an enemy scope, or a strange blink from a partner right before the handshake. Spotting danger is one thing. Reacting in time is another.

epccg.high_levels: you're frighteningly fast and never caught flat-footed. But reacting that fast makes you look plainly impatient, and plenty of times reacting fast just makes things go wrong faster.
epccg.good_for: gamers, sailors, gunners, every other kind of -er, gamblers.
epccg.bad_for: calm people, people who need to save face, anyone who doesn't want to look like they're on speed.

Back when I worked the city, I'd swipe a bank card out of some guy's pocket and that was dinner sorted. Back then I still had Travis to crack the cards... People call it petty theft, but the trade takes real skill. First you learn to walk in step with the crowd and spot which pocket bulges most. Then you work out how much weight to slip back in so they don't notice the coins have flown. If you don't know how, don't mess around. The old men at the guard post started carrying shock batons last week, and it hurts like you wouldn't believe.

quote: Yes, yes, a watchmaker and a gunsmith aren't far apart. Lay every part of a pendulum clock on the table and odds are your brain starts shorting out. Guns are the same: picking one up and shooting is a world away from stripping every screw and putting it back. Anyone can read a clock, but how many can fix one? What you need is someone who sees every piece of the puzzle and joins them into one. Like me! Unless you use a digital clock or one of those toy guns from the carnival stalls, in which case: scram. Shoo, shoo.
epccg.intro: Acuity is your grasp of complex mechanisms, from something as small as a stopwatch to something as huge as a transcontinental cannon. All of it can be taken apart by you.

quote: Fine, if you insist, I'll review all the evidence. Aaaand there's nothing worth reviewing. The dashcam at 11:45 shows, plain as day, the defendant stabbing a man to death. And I'm sick of your take-the-punch-take-the-bribe attitude, Your Honour, and your jury's too. The evidence is right there, so why no arrest? Because the defendant comes from a good family? Or because the pile of cash under the table is just too hard to pass up? You know what? As counsel for the plaintiff, I'm going to walk outside and tell the world I won. There is only one truth, and if you disagree it's because you're a pack of nitpicking self-servers. I WIN. BYE-BYE. CLOSE THE COURT.

quote: I asked whether he'd like a glass of water or anything. Honestly, officers, that afternoon was the first time I'd met Mr. Duboi, and everything in my statement is true. Granted, keeping an electric chair in one's office isn't for everyone, but I'm a lover of the arts. I adore bold, satirical work; how could I not display one of the masterpieces of my collection? It was a regrettable accident. That chair was never used until Mr. Duboi volunteered himself into it. How was I to know he would switch the power on himself and die so needlessly? Tell the court I'll be there. A gentleman like me never passes up a conversation he is certain to win.

epccg.speaker: Paul Remarque
quote: I'd rather have been the one who took the bullet, you understand? Operation Daggerfall really did change the course of history. I know. I was there. What they praise and trumpet is partly true. But what they forgot? Too much.
I saw the eyes of a boy, sixteen or so, half burned black, lying still two metres above a pool of blood. What was he thinking before judgment day?

I saw the eyes of a father, half red, half black, fingers trembling as he cradled the body of a Crawler smaller than the rest. Right before Captain Kain called in another barrage. What was he thinking before those deafening blasts?

I saw. Horror... horror and pain, grief and helplessness. Oh, I'd give my whole fortune to forget, you understand? Forget the horror in their eyes, the horror I still feel in my chest, the horror no words can describe. The horror of an empty face hanging above an iron stake.

quote: Jazmine, Jazmine of the dying afternoon, lead the lost soul away from breaking.

Ask ten people in the recon squad and nine won't want to share a transport with me. They say the way I talk isn't easy on the ears. I can rarely sit with someone ten minutes before something about them grates on me, and saying it plainly would be a little... vulgar. So I use metaphor. A faint sweat stain becomes 'the perfume of corpse-flowers in the Sonz marsh.' An uncleaned rifle becomes 'a homemade death at dawn.' I won't hide it: watching them fume without a comeback always brightens my heart a little.

I've lived alone between earth and sky too long for one or two more haters to matter. But Jazmine is something else. Coarse as an old man from Chezknov, and yet sometimes... gentle as a golden lotus in a stinking marsh. Can your smile melt my heart? Hard to say. The one thing I know for certain: you make me want to be a better man.

Mother wanted to know, to understand, to hold the chance to prove it true. And after more than a hundred years of study, they chose Mother for this seat. The one who makes the unreal real.

epccg.effect: Karma moves 1 further each time it changes: more when it is awarded, more when it is taken. Your Order Call reaches 1 tile further. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
epccg.high_levels: people mistake you for a general, a leader or a top CEO, which raises the odds you get investigated and make the news for buying apples at the market instead of the supermarket.
epccg.good_for: soldiers, police, security, teachers, anyone who has to be cool.
epccg.bad_for: sugar babies, fuckboys (you risk ending up married instead of a one-night stand).
